_purpose: ✒️ Executive Enactment Record — the count-summary vocabulary. The EER carries NO score and NO percentage, so this is what occupies the slot where the 🏛️ lane prints a percentage: the same information a ratio would compress, published uncompressed.
framing: Of the formal actions on file
_framingWhy: Not a disclaimer in small type — the FIRST clause of the sentence, in the same type size as the numbers. It is what makes the counts true: the denominator is our file, not the figure's complete output. A reader who takes N for 'everything they did' has been misled by omission even though every individual number is correct. Precedent: consistency.js:1905 _orMappedSummaryTip already names the records it did NOT count.
_framingRule: Every rendered label MUST begin with this literal string. Asserted as a prefix, not matched as a pattern, so a count interpolated into the middle of it cannot quietly break the lead-in.

issues._why: Axis A — alignment between a stated position and the formal actions on file. One issue is aligned, against, or both.

noActionFound.label: stated position, no action found
noActionFound._why: COVERAGE, never a negative. Folding this into `against` would convert 'we have found no action' into 'they acted against it'. The app cannot prove a negative over an unbounded action space, so this is reported on its own line and is never summed into against.

noStance.label: action on file, no stated position
noStance._why: Also covers a stated position of 'mixed': a non-directional stance gives an action nothing to be checked against, which is what this bucket means.

actions._why: Axis B — what happened to the action afterwards. One document has exactly one current standing (the latest vr_exec_action_status row by effective_at). No congressional counterpart exists; this axis is why the EER cannot be a re-skin of the 🏛️ lane.

challengedUnverified.label: challenged in court — no ruling on file
challengedUnverified._why: A live challenge with no primary ruling we have read. It is NOT a claim that the action was blocked and NOT a claim that it survived — it is the honest name for the gap between the two, and it exists so that gap does not have to be filed as `in_force`. Filing a challenged order as `in_force` is the quiet error this token prevents: `in_force` is a positive claim that nothing has disturbed the order, and a court that has not ruled has not confirmed that. Contested, because a reader who sees only `in_force` counts is told the record is settled when it is not.
challengedUnverified._useRule: Only where we have (a) a primary court document establishing the challenge is on file and live, and (b) no primary ruling resolving it. If a primary ruling exists, read it and use the token it supports — this is never a shortcut for 'we did not check'.

_unitsWhy: THE TRAP THIS FILE EXISTS TO STOP. Axis A counts issues; Axis B counts documents. One signed law can touch five issues and one issue can have three orders behind it, so a row reading '3 aligned · 4 in force' invites the reader to treat 3 and 4 as parts of one whole. Shipping the unit as DATA — rather than leaving it implicit in variable names — is what makes the check mechanical: any renderer that adds an issue-unit count to a document-unit count is caught by construction.

labelTemplates.coverageGap: {noActionFound} {issueWord} with a stated position and no action found.

_emptyWhy: Nothing on file returns an empty string and lets the panel's own no_record state speak, following the existing precedent at consistency.js:1895 that 'a member with no record shows no claim about one'. The summary never manufactures a sentence to fill space.
_thinRecordWhy: One or two actions cannot carry a pattern. Adopted from _orMappedSummaryText, which already appends 'so far — still a thin record' at low N so a count does not read as depth it does not have.
_standingAlwaysVisibleWhy: If any action is contested, the standing clause survives into EVERY rendering including the most compact chip. A summary showing only alignment implies the whole record is operative — the exact failure the second axis exists to prevent, reintroduced at the aggregate level after being solved at the card level. challengedUnverified is on this list for the same reason it is `contested`: dropping it would leave the compact rendering saying 'in force' about a record with a live unresolved challenge in it.
_defaultTermScopeWhy: An all-time count mixes terms and a reader takes an old action as current. The default rendering is the current term; the all-time count is available in the tip. Changing the denominator is the one thing that must never happen quietly, so both figures are always reachable.

_why.%: Decision 1: no percentage on the EER, ever. A president's set of possible orders is unbounded and self-selected, so any ratio would divide by a number we invented.
_why.gradedAdjectives: 'Mostly acted on it' IS a percentage — a ratio judgment wearing a word. It reintroduces through the copy the invented denominator the no-score rule removed from the math, and it would pass every numeric check. The label describes composition; it never grades it.
_why.proportionWords: most / majority / half / few / many are ratios in prose.
_why.voteWords: Decision 9: no vote language on any EER surface. This figure cast no floor votes.

forbidden._scopeWarning: This pattern deliberately matches `consistent` and `mixed`, which are LEGITIMATE tokens and labels in consistency.js's VERDICTS table for the 🏛️ lane. The matcher must therefore be applied to EER strings ONLY. scripts/test-exec-vocab.mjs asserts both directions: the EER vocabulary is clean, AND the pattern still fires on 'Mixed record' so it can never become vacuous.
